subject: Residency operator verification & SIG/CAIQ addendum
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthvera.com>, HealthVera Security <compliance@healthvera.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthvera.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency operator verification & SIG/CAIQ addendum

Elena / HealthVera team,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As discussed, HealthVera's legal/security team asked for a compact evidence packet so your compliance reviewers can sign off on the EU-only deployment with private connectivity. To keep this narrow and operationally useful, can you confirm the items below? We can deliver everything in the next 48 hours once we have your acceptance of the scope.

Requested items (target: EU-only private deployment with no cross-border egress):
- Operator roster: names, role (operator / on-call / SRE), and whether accounts require bastion access. A CSV format is fine.
- Keystore operator model: confirmation that keystore splits are enforced (operator split + HSM) and list of operator IDs who can request key rotation.
- Private endpoint egress mapping: short text trace for a sample request showing the VPC peering path and any hops to third parties.
- SIG/CAIQ addendum: We will map our CAIQ control IDs to HealthVera requirements, but please flag any control areas you want expanded (e.g., cryptographic key custody, operator access).
- Short statement on retention: confirmation that logs for admin/operator sessions are retained for at least 12 months for EU tenants.

Attachments we plan to send: sig-caiq-addendum.pdf (mapping + clarifications), keystore-operator-roster.csv (redacted demo), egress-flow-trace.txt (anonymized trace).

If this scope looks right, reply and we’ll push the packet and a short runbook for your ops team. If you prefer a granular SOC 2 artifact instead of the addendum, say so and we’ll attach the SOC 2 artifact list.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthvera.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthVera Security <compliance@healthvera.com>, Procurement <procurement@healthvera.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency operator verification & SIG/CAIQ addendum

Markus —

Thanks, this is exactly the level we were hoping for. A few clarifying Qs before you send artifacts: 
1) For the operator roster CSV, please include a column indicating whether the operator has MFA enforced and whether their access requires ticket approval (ok to redact emails).
2) For the keystore model, HealthVera requires confirmation that key material for EU tenants is never exported to non-EU HSMs. A short line on geo-boundary for key material would be helpful.
3) For private endpoint flow, can you provide a single sample showing private peering (no NAT traversal) and confirm the egress firewall rules that block public internet egress by default?

Procurement: we may need a short statement for our vendor pack that references your CAIQ mapping.

If you can send the packet by EOD Monday (20 Sep), we’ll prioritize review.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security Programs
HealthVera Health
elena@healthvera.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency operator verification & SIG/CAIQ addendum

Markus / Ben —

On this. I will assemble the operator roster and the keystore statement. Quick notes for the artifacts: 
- keystore-operator-roster.csv: include columns (OperatorID, Role, MFA_enforced:yes/no, Ticket_required:yes/no, Bastion_access:yes/no). We’ll redact direct emails and include HR job codes instead of names if they prefer.
- sig-caiq-addendum.pdf: I’ll pull our existing CAIQ mapping and add two callouts for EU-only key custody and for the private peering egress rules.
- egress-flow-trace.txt: I’ll generate an anonymized 5-step trace from request->privatelink->egress-filter that demonstrates no public internet hop.

Ben: can you attach the excerpt from our SOC 2 evidence binder (admin session logs retention) so we can reference it if HealthVera asks for SOC artifacts? If you don’t want to attach the whole binder, a one-page excerpt is fine.

I’ll aim to have the draft packet and Drive link ready by Monday morning (20 Sep) for Markus to review.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance Operations
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@healthvera.com>, HealthVera Security <compliance@healthvera.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency operator verification & SIG/CAIQ addendum

Elena —

Appreciate the clarifying questions. We attached the initial packet to this message (three files). Summary of responses inline below and links to the Drive folder if your team prefers to review there: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_keystore_ops

- Operator roster (keystore-operator-roster.csv): includes OperatorID, Role, MFA_enforced, Ticket_required, Bastion_access. We redacted personal emails and included HR job codes.
- Keystore geo-boundary: key material for EU tenants is generated/held in EU HSM partitions and never exported to non-EU HSMs. The sig-caiq-addendum.pdf contains the formal custody statement (see section 2.1).
- Private endpoint flow (egress-flow-trace.txt): sample trace attached showing VPC peering -> privatelink -> destination within EU cloud region. Egress firewall rules: default-deny egress profile applied to tenant subnets; explicit allow required for any external destinations.
- Retention: admin/operator session logs retained 12 months; excerpts from our SOC 2 binder are referenced in the addendum.

Attachments in this message: keystore-operator-roster.csv (CSV), sig-caiq-addendum.pdf (PDF), egress-flow-trace.txt (TXT). If you want a deeper SOC 2 artifact, we can produce a one-page excerpt under an NDA/secure link.

Would you prefer acceptance as a single confirmation email from HealthVera security or a short signoff form we can route through DocuSign? We can send a signoff form and a mutual non-disclosure for the SOC artifacts.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Compliance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
